message.content: In Christian tradition, the emphasis is usually placed on Jesus Christ as the central and ultimate figure—often referred to as the “Son of God” and the fulfillment of prophetic expectations. However, many Christians also regard earlier prophets from the Hebrew Scriptures (Old Testament) as significant, such as Moses, who led the Israelites out of Egypt; Isaiah, whose writings are seen as prophetic of the Messiah; and others like Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and Daniel. Different Christian traditions may highlight different figures or emphasize the continuity between Old Testament prophets and the New Testament revelation. Ultimately, the importance of a particular prophet can vary depending on theological perspective, denominational teachings, and individual belief.
